originality.rationale: Claim is r>=3 full finite cycle covariance in the unconditioned configuration pairing, including arbitrary degree sequences and entire regular sign spectrum. McKay–Wormald–Wysocka (2004) analyzes asymptotic short cycles for simple random regular graphs (where loops do not exist), while Janson (2006) gives different loop/double-edge moment statements. An accessible earlier local result gives r=2 loop/parallel-pair covariance and is explicitly excluded. Distinguishing full r>=3 cycle-count covariance and spanning-cycle exception is neither identical to nor directly entailed by those prior claims. Residual obscure-literature and inaccessible-1981 risks are stated, not suppressed.
residual_risks: A historical pairing-model theorem might contain the mixed r>=3 moment under different wording and might subsume this calculation; targeted searches are not proof of absolute novelty.
The 1981 Wormald short-cycle article is not available in full in this environment and was not treated as a whole-document noncoverage.
An earlier exact two-edge multicycle (parallel pair) calculation shares the method; the present value lies in complete r>=3 spectrum and boundary classification, not a new counting technique.

value.rationale: This is a complete cycle-length dependence profile for the natural pairing model. The sign changes at the structural d=2/d>=3 boundary simultaneously for every nonspanning cycle length, whereas the unique full spanning d=2 cycle has the opposite sign. The exact arbitrary-degree formula and distinct n^-2 versus n^-1 covariance scales provide finite and asymptotic quantitative dependence unavailable from cycle marginals or Poisson limits alone. This is a motivated structural sign classification; the r=2 known case is not claimed as an increment, and only one unified theorem is presented.
